newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel maintains recent recovery.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel maintains recent recovery.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market which has emerged from recent sluggishness continued its gradual recovery, led by the strength of the swaps market, traders said.

They said physical fundamentals have not changed with Chinese authorities bent on snuffing out smuggling and severely curbing legal imports, but the market was being propped up by speculation in the swaps market led by a major and western traders.
They said players were trading on the east-west spread--buying the east and selling the west--to position themselves for possible cargo movements westward.

Swaps gas oil for September traded at $22.78, $22.75 and $22.70 and was last indicated lower at $22.60/$22.65, up 15 cents from Thursday. August traded at $21.75 and was last quoted at $21.75/$21.80, also up 15 cents.
A 150,000-barrel physical gas oil cargo was traded between two European majors at a 40-cent-per-barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes for August 2-6 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis.

The buyer said the reason they bought on a floating price basis was because they expected values in August to slip further because of weak fundamentals in East Asia Asia and the MidEast. Offers for first half August were earlier seen as high as $21.70 per barrel but was later lowered to around $20.90-$21.20.

With China's continued absence, the market again looked towards India to provide some support. State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a tender to buy 0.5 and 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil for deliveries in September.

The tender closes on July 31 and offers will be valid until August 1. IOC's purchase of 165,000 tonne for August deliveries early this month had sent the market tumbling until offers hit a bottom of $19.50 per barrel before crawling up.
Jet fuel remained steady as a Singapore trader was said to be pricing its July cargoes into Indonesia. Indonesia was said to be seeking about two million barrels for August deliveries.
But traders said the fundamentals on jet are even worse than gas oil and they consider the current jet/gas oil spread to be too wide and should be limited to around $1.00 per barrel.
On Friday, 100,000 barrels of jet fuel was sold by a European major to a Singapore trader at $23.30 per barrel for August 8-12 lifting fob, 20 cents below the last deal on Wednesday.
